newsitem.title: JAPAN: Share trade by ex-MOF official regrettable -- Kubo.
newsitem.headline: Share trade by ex-MOF official regrettable -- Kubo.

text.p: The involvement of a former Finance Ministry official in the reported purchase of shares of a consumer credit company is very regrettable, Finance Minister Wataru Kubo said on Friday.

The national financial daily, Nihon Keizai Shimbun, reported that a former finance ministry official, who was the head of the ministry's banking bureau, purchased shares of consumer credit firm Takefuji before the shares were registered on the OTC market.
Kubo said the former official used the name of his daughter to purchase the shares.
"He is a former official who left the ministry nearly 20 years ago. But it is very regrettable that a top official used someone else's name to do the share deal," Kubo said.
Although the official has left the ministry, he is a member of the financial system council, an advisory panel to the finance minister.
Kubo said the official, who is also an advisor to one of Japan's major securities firms, would be asked to leave the financial system council immediately.
The Finance Ministry has come under attack in recent years for its cosy relationship with the financial industry.
